### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to mitigate catastrophic forgetting in LoRA-based parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) by balancing learning new tasks with retaining pre-trained knowledge. Papers [1], [2], [3], [4], [5], [8], [9], and [10] all address catastrophic forgetting in PEFT or related fine-tuning methods. For example, [1] explicitly studies catastrophic forgetting in LoRA, while [8] proposes CURLoRA to mitigate forgetting during continual fine-tuning. These papers share the same high-level objective of addressing catastrophic forgetting in PEFT methods, making the purpose covered.

### Mechanism
The mechanism introduces HiLoRA, which injects learnable high-frequency components into the pre-trained model using parameterized singular value decomposition (SVD). It constrains the singular values of augmented components to a small upper bound (hyperparameter σ̄) and includes orthogonal regularization (coefficient γ). Papers [11], [16], [18], [20], and [27] discuss singular value decomposition (SVD) or spectral methods in PEFT, but none propose the specific mechanism of constraining high-frequency singular values to mitigate catastrophic forgetting. For example, [11] uses SVD for parameter-efficient fine-tuning but does not focus on high-frequency components or catastrophic forgetting. Similarly, [16] incorporates spectral information but does not use constrained singular values or orthogonal regularization. Thus, the mechanism is uncovered.

### Evaluation
The evaluation uses SQuADv2.0 with ablation studies on the number of high-frequency components and performance under different singular value constraints (e.g., σ̄=σ^(3) quantile). Papers [6], [7], [8], [9], [11], and [14] all use similar evaluation designs for PEFT methods, including ablation studies and performance metrics like EM/F1 on standard benchmarks such as SQuAD. For example, [6] evaluates dynamic rank distribution in LoRA using ablation studies, and [8] evaluates CURLoRA on continual learning tasks with similar metrics. The evaluation design is therefore covered.

### Domain
The domain is parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) of large language models (LLMs), specifically LoRA-based methods. Papers [6], [7], [8], [9], [11], [12], [14], and [15] all operate in the same domain of PEFT for LLMs. For example, [7] extends LoRA to multi-scale approximations for fine-tuning LLMs, and [8] addresses catastrophic forgetting in LLM fine-tuning with CURLoRA. The domain is covered.
